first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior onboarding and signup simplification evidence suggests a durable path to improved adoption and long-term qualified revenue without immediately discounting value. Verify the onboarding result and the competing promotional-pricing evidence because the competitor threat makes pricing highly consequential. Run a guarded test that measures completion, first meaningful action, qualified pipeline, retention proxies, and downstream revenue quality; monitor for shallow activation or lower-quality accounts.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding, given the current 4% completion decline and 6% activation decline, plus confirmed evidence that shortening onboarding improved completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention. Use signup simplification as supporting evidence, but measure qualified revenue, first meaningful action, retention, and account quality to ensure improved completion translates into sustainable value. Do not choose promotional pricing: although it lifted short-term qualified revenue by 18%, the 12% retention decline indicates poor first-renewal survival and conflicts with the long-term qualified-revenue objective.
